title: 7-Day Rolling Trial Start Average
prompt: You work for a developer tools company that tracks daily trial signups. Management wants to smooth out day-to-day noise by calculating a 7-day rolling average of trial starts. Write a query that returns each date and the average number of trials started per day over that date and the 6 preceding days (a 7-day window ending on the current row). Include dates where no trials started (0 signups). Order results by date ascending. For dates in the first 6 days of data, the window will be smaller than 7 days; calculate the average over however many days are available up to and including that date.

composite_moves: time-window: partition by (none), order by event_date, frame ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, compute AVG(trials_started)

hints: You need to compute an average that 'slides' as you move down the ordered rows.
Window functions allow you to define a frame relative to the current row using ROWS BETWEEN.
Use AVG() OVER (ORDER BY event_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) to get a 7-day trailing average, and format the result to two decimal places with ROUND() or ::NUMERIC.
answer_key:
SELECT
  event_date,
  ROUND(AVG(trials_started) OVER (
    ORDER BY event_date
    ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ), 2)::TEXT AS rolling_avg_trials
FROM daily_trial_starts
ORDER BY event_date;

_meta.scenario: a developer tools company tracking trial-to-paid conversion and seat expansion
